subject: docs/coop/artifacts/platform-tcb-contract.v5.json

blockers.title: The Linux selector still collapses distinct host-ABI TCBs into one qualified platform profile
evidence: For Linux, the only new scheme is linux-uname-release: a kernel release string from uname -r. The other required members are merely osFamily=linux, architecture, and filesystem. No distribution/publisher, userspace release, or attested platform-image variant participates in the key even though this TCB expressly governs the loader, libc, certificate store, font, ICU, and comparable userspace dependencies.

The grammar does not bind an identifierScheme to osFamily. An EXACT-BUILD object using macos-product-build is syntactically lawful in a Linux profile, and linux-uname-release is syntactically lawful in a macOS profile; the later packet is forbidden to mint the missing compatibility rule.

Two Linux hosts can therefore have the same four required members and different material userspace TCBs. relationToEveryTcbEntry keys both allowlists by that same profile, and g22VersusQualified attaches qualification to that profile. The contract can only union their members under one qualified key or make one host unrepresentable; it cannot qualify the two TCBs independently.
blockers.impact: A host that was not the environment exercised by G22 can select the same qualified profile as the tested host. If both variants are supported, an object declared for one variant is no longer undeclared or identity drift on the other, defeating the profile boundary the negative tests are meant to prove.
blockers.requiredRepair: Make the contract-owned platformProfile key distinguish every material host-ABI equivalence class. Bind each identifierScheme to its lawful osFamily and canonical trusted observation source. For Linux, include a closed publisher/distribution plus userspace-release or equivalent attested platform-image discriminator in addition to any kernel-release selector. The later population packet may choose values but must not define these semantics.

shouldFix.title: The SONAME-ABI companion still has no closed encoding inside either lawful libc authenticity payload
shouldFix.evidence: A signed entry still carries exactly one classMap tag, and libc classMap lawfully selects only PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND. V5 adds prose saying SONAME-ABI is inside either payload and not a signed-entry field, but neither authenticity tag declares an optional SONAME field, payload key, object shape, or cardinality. SONAME-ABI remains a sibling under tags. notASignedEntryField closes one invalid encoding without defining a conforming encoding.
shouldFix.impact: One producer can omit the companion, another can invent an unrostered payload member, and another can treat the sibling tag as a nested tagged union. The authenticity requirement itself remains sound, but the signed inventory shape is not interoperably deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Either delete SONAME-ABI companion language, or define a named optional field with a closed object shape, such as sonameAbi: { soname, abiSelector }, inside the PLATFORM-ATTESTED and DIGEST-BOUND libc payload schemas, with extra forms rejected and the existing non-identity comparison rule retained.

measurements.check: Closed and collision-resistant platform selector semantics
measurements.evidence: EXACT-BUILD now has exact comparison and CLOSED-RANGE is prohibited, but linux-uname-release does not distinguish userspace/platform variants and no scheme-to-osFamily constraint exists. See PTCB-V5-B1.
Libc authenticity remains PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND and SONAME cannot be sole identity, but neither lawful payload declares the purported optional companion field. See PTCB-V5-S1.

measurements.check: CLOSED-RANGE prohibition and filesystem escape structure
measurements.evidence: CLOSED-RANGE expressly cannot occupy supportedVersionOrBuildSelector. OTHER-FSTYPE fixes the tag, sha-256 algorithm id, UTF-8 NFC hash input, 64-character lowercase-hex encoding, length, and equality inputs. The structural range and filesystem halves of PTCB-V4-B1 are repaired.

measurements.check: Exhaustive signed entry and declared-versus-ambient predicate
measurements.evidence: identityRuleShape.declared and signedEntry.required agree on exactly four exhaustive fields. environmentInfluence remains a closed FIXED/FORBIDDEN map; unnamed influence and mutable PATH/loader substitution refuse.

The observation boundary still covers every actual attempt, capture is independent of the tested process, lifecycle and sensor-health closure are required, retained events bind subject/profile/carrier/process/class/outcome, and false-match use fails.

measurements.check: One carrier, population reservation, and carrier-absence consequence
measurements.evidence: One DR-101 successor owns exactly one inventory copy; DR-103 consumes it; ceremony is separate; and G22 cannot QUALIFY without it. All four stems keep both selector members RESERVED and required before freeze; no later packet or owner is designated.

The subject binds NOTHING, is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and DO-NOT-SEAL, leaves DR-126 OPEN, populates no per-OS members, excludes language-runtime/Node from the core taxonomy, re-owns neither DR-G07 nor D-006 numbers, creates no D-096 (A) grant, and authorizes no implementation.

attacks.attack: EXACT-BUILD schemes distinguish every qualified platform TCB and are compatible with osFamily
attacks.evidence: Exact equality and range prohibition landed, but Linux kernel release is not a userspace/platform variant and schemes are not bound to osFamily. See PTCB-V5-B1.

attacks.attack: SONAME-ABI is a closed optional subfield rather than a fifth field or sole identity tag
attacks.evidence: The fifth-field and sole-authenticity paths are prohibited, but no lawful authenticity payload contains a defined companion field. See PTCB-V5-S1.

attacks.attack: CLOSED-RANGE remains usable or OTHER-FSTYPE lacks algorithm, encoding, or digest length
attacks.evidence: The range tag is prohibited as a required member, and OTHER-FSTYPE supplies a fixed algorithm id plus exact lowercase-hex digest input and length rules.

attacks.attack: A three-field entry survives or naming PATH/loader influence makes mutable substitution lawful
attacks.evidence: The declared and detailed shapes agree on four exhaustive fields, while environment influence accepts only fixed signed values or refusal.

attacks.attack: Capture can self-assert completeness, omit actual attempts, or use a false evidence join
attacks.evidence: Independent capture, lifecycle/sensor-health closure, independently checkable inapplicability proof, retained bindings, and false-match failure remain mandatory.

attacks.attack: Carrier ownership is joint or absent without blocking G22
attacks.evidence: Field authorship remains singular, consumers and ceremony are separate, and absence expressly prevents qualification.

attacks.attack: The v4-to-v5 path contains an unrostered semantic change
attacks.evidence: All 38 changed semantic nodes are under rostered or succession-metadata paths; reviewGuidance is append-only and slice1ProfileStems is now expressly rostered.

attacks.attack: The candidate populates platform tables, designates a later packet, expands the core TCB, satisfies DR-126, qualifies G22, or grants application/implementation authority
attacks.evidence: Selectors and members remain RESERVED, the packet is indefinite, scope remains narrow, DR-126 remains OPEN, G22 remains unqualified, and every application or implementation claim is denied.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. linux-uname-release still allows distinct userspace/host-ABI TCBs to share one qualified profile and identifier schemes are not bound to osFamily. SONAME-ABI also remains without a closed lawful payload field. DR-126 remains OPEN; no D-096 (A) grant, satisfaction, qualification, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
